title: BACK IN TIME - 1976: UFO leaves state police, others stumped

Published 2:32 pm Wednesday, September 2, 2026

By Central Oregonian

100 years ago

September 9, 1926

Prineville and the surrounding scenery is in the films at last. Through the instrumentality of the Buick promotion service and in response to the efforts of Charles A. Ross of the Inland Motor Company, the dream of Prineville boosters has been realized.

A large part of last week, Ed Knox, serviceman for the Howard Automobile Company of Portland, and Brownell, cameraman in the employ of Buick people, made 425 feet of a film depicting the unusual uses to which Buick cars are put. Under direction of Mr. Ross, they visited Summit Prairie and filmed the white-faced cattle on several ranches there with Buick cars modestly displayed in the background of the picture as the picturesque cattleman quitted the saddle to hurry home for a late lunch or sped away to lease new pastures or sell his growing herds on a high but fast-changing market.

75 years ago

September 6, 1951

Fred Cuthbert, landscape architect from the University of Oregon, was in Prineville Friday to discuss plans for the proposed city park with members of the park commission.

Mr. Cuthbert drew up the preliminary plans for the proposed park, to be located between Elm and Juniper streets and between Fourth and Seventh streets several years ago.

The park commission also discussed designs for the proposed city swimming pool with Mr. Cuthbert. He recommended a T- or L-shaped pool or a separate diving pool. The commission decided to invite an engineer from one of the principal pool designing firms in the country to discuss further designs.

50 years ago

September 9, 1976

An unidentified flying object (UFO) was reported southeast of Ochoco Reservoir Monday evening, but an immediate search turned up nothing.

Two officers of the Oregon State Police cited what they thought was a burning plane in the Gerow Butte area and felt that it was on a downward path.

On the assumption that a plane had caught fire and crashed, Alex Koldea, of Rimrock Aviation, was asked to fly a search mission to determine the location of the plane. Two different flights turned up nothing.

The Oregon State Forestry Department was asked to alert their lookouts in the area and attempt to spot the flame. Their efforts also proved fruitless!

Corporal Don Bussey of the Oregon State Police described the sighting as a meteor or satellite or other phenomenon.

Sighting of the fiery object was made in Madras, at Smith Rock State Park, east of Ochoco Reservoir and as far east as Prairie City.

State police checked with the Federal Aviation Administration, which also received many calls, and the FAA stated that there were no planes unaccounted for.

25 years ago

September 6, 2001

As expected, the July financial report from the City of Prineville Railroad was not full of good news. The monthly report from the other municipal enterprise, Meadow Lakes, was slightly better.

Both reports were presented to the city council this week. COP-RR manager Jerry Price labeled his report by calling it a “sorry financial statement.” City councilmember Dorless Reid was understanding: “Jerry, if you don’t have anything to move, you can’t move it.”

The council’s railroad committee, made up of Price and members of the council, have been gathering information aimed at helping the elected body make decisions on the railroad’s future. Mayor Steve Uffelman, a member of that committee, told other council members that a plan is being developed. “A plan of action,” he explained, “that will cover the next three months and the next six months.”
